source_excerpt: India vs New Zealand: Ishan Kishan ruled out of 2nd T20I after injury, Kumar Kushagra added as cover left Ishan Kishan hurt himself in the first T20I. ANI ANI https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/psf17g/article71614552.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/20261022082L.jpg ANI Christchurch [New Zealand], Oct 22 (ANI): India's Ishan Kishan warms up for the 1st T20I match against New Zealand at Hagley Oval, in Christchurch on Thursday. (ANI Photo) Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I against New Zealand after sustaining a low-grade right adductor strain in the series opener. Ishan Kishan is ruled out of the second T20I against New Zealand due to a low grade right adductor strain, which he sustained during the first T20I of the series. The BCCI Medical Team is monitoring his progress. 24-year-old Jharkhand wicketkeeper batter Kumar Kushagra has been added as cover for Kishan. Kushagra is a part of the squad for first two India A games, and has played a handful of IPL matches for Delhi Capitals and Gujarat Titans. India’s successful chase of 226 in the first T20I against New Zealand, sealed with four wickets and two balls to spare, was not without its talking points. Tilak Varma walking in at No. 3 ahead of Ishan raised a few eyebrows, adding an intriguing subplot to an otherwise thrilling run chase. Tilak struggled to find his rhythm, managing just six off 11 balls before falling to Michael Bracewell. Meanwhile. Ishan lasted only three deliveries for a solitary run before Mitchell Santner sent him back. The second T20I is tomorrow (Oct 24) in Christchurch.
